Option 3: "beh rooz faten-e naghban-e miyeh and ham-e - beh buستان-e vatan sarv va susan and ham-e". On the day of calamity, all are guardians of the homeland. Option 4: "gharīb-e rā del-e sergašte ba vatan bāshad - hayā-ye kuy-e to az sar namarad bīرون". The stranger's heart is torn from the homeland. The breeze of your courtyard never leaves the heart. It's more about the duty and its consequences rather than the emotional or symbolic bonds. So Option 2 might be the odd one out.
